name: Context7
description: Pull up-to-date, version-specific docs for libraries and frameworks.
summary: Pulls up-to-date, version-specific docs for libraries and frameworks.
package: Context7 hosted remote MCP server (no local install); local fallback: @upstash/context7-mcp via npx

Fallback if you prefer a local process: replace the entry with command `npx`, args ["-y", "@upstash/context7-mcp"]. Source: https://github.com/upstash/context7.

summary: Structured step-by-step reasoning scratchpad for hard problems.

name: Roblox Studio
description: Connect an AI client to a live Roblox Studio session — explore the data model, write Luau, and run/test in play mode.
summary: Connects an AI client to a live Roblox Studio session to explore and script it.
note: Uses Roblox's built-in Studio MCP server (the community Rust server, Roblox/studio-rust-mcp-server, was archived 2026-04-03). In Studio: Assistant > ... > Manage MCP Servers > turn on "Enable Studio as MCP server", then restart Studio. Per-OS commands: Windows `cmd.exe /c %LOCALAPPDATA%\Roblox\mcp.bat` (cmd.exe expands %LOCALAPPDATA% at launch, so no user path is stored) and macOS `/Applications/RobloxStudio.app/Contents/MacOS/StudioMCP`. Roblox documents no Linux command, so install is skipped on Linux. Studio's Assistant Settings > MCP Servers also offers quick connect for Claude Code. A committed .mcp.json keeps the OS command of whoever installed it, so teammates on another OS should reinstall this server from the panel.
package: Roblox Studio's built-in MCP server (no separate install)
dataNote: Bridges an AI client to your local Roblox Studio session; the AI can read your place's data model and write/run Luau code in it.

name: Unity AI Assistant MCP (Official · Unity 6+)
description: Unity's official MCP bridge, provided by the Unity AI Assistant package (com.unity.ai.assistant). Lets an MCP client such as Claude Code drive the Unity Editor: manage scenes, GameObjects, and assets.
summary: Unity's official editor MCP bridge via the Unity AI Assistant package (Unity 6000.0+).
note: Requires Unity 6 (6000.0) or later with the com.unity.ai.assistant package installed. In Unity, open Edit > Project Settings > AI > Unity MCP Server and confirm the bridge shows Running. Unity's setup page does not state account requirements; check Unity's AI Assistant terms for any Unity Cloud project or beta opt-in your account needs. The first connection shows Pending Connection in that settings page - choose Accept. Per-OS relay (Claude Code expands USERPROFILE/HOME at launch): Windows `${USERPROFILE}\.unity\relay\relay_win.exe`, macOS Apple Silicon `${HOME}/.unity/relay/relay_mac_arm64.app/Contents/MacOS/relay_mac_arm64`, Linux `${HOME}/.unity/relay/relay_linux`, all with `--mcp`. Unity's page lists only an Apple Silicon macOS binary; Intel Macs are UNVERIFIED (no documented binary), and the page shows the Linux path as `~/.unity/relay/relay_linux` (converted to ${HOME} here; Unity's explicit Linux config block is UNVERIFIED). A committed .mcp.json keeps the OS command of whoever installed it, so teammates on another OS should reinstall this server from the panel.
package: Unity AI Assistant package com.unity.ai.assistant (relay binary installed under ~/.unity/relay/)
dataNote: Local relay between your MCP client and your open Unity Editor; the AI can read and modify the open project's scenes and assets. Unity approves each new client connection inside the editor.

name: UEFN Bridge (Trashbyrd's Power Tools)
description: Live UEFN editor control from Claude — read/set actor properties, run audits, and browse materials, textures, and the level via Trashbyrd's Power Tools.
summary: Live UEFN editor control from Claude via Trashbyrd's Power Tools.
note: Install Power Tools yourself, then add it to your OWN .mcp.json (see .mcp.json.example in this repo). Download the release from GitHub Releases below and unzip it, then set `<POWER_TOOLS_DIR>` in the command args to that folder's full path (forward slashes even on Windows). Env vars per Power Tools' INSTALL.md: UEFN_BRIDGE_DIR is the bridge IPC directory shared by the MCP server and the in-UEFN Python bridge — must be set for both sides or neither, or they land in different directories (defaults to a per-machine temp dir if unset); UEFN_VERSE_PROJECT_DIR points at UEFN's VerseProject data root (digests, .vproject files); VERSE_LSP_PATH and VERSE_LSP_CHECK_SCRIPT are only needed for the uefn_verse_check tool. No env block is required in most client configs.
package: Trashbyrd's Power Tools (downloaded release, run via `node`; not published to npm)
dataNote: Runs locally; bridges Claude to your open UEFN session over temp-file IPC. No external/network calls.

name: Unreal Engine MCP (Official · UE 5.8+)
description: Epic's official in-editor MCP server, built into Unreal Editor 5.8+. Enable the "Unreal MCP" and "All Toolsets" plugins and toggle Auto Start Server in Editor Preferences, then connect over HTTP/SSE. For general Unreal Engine projects — distinct from the UEFN Bridge above, which targets UEFN/Fortnite.
summary: Epic's official in-editor MCP server, built into Unreal Editor 5.8+.
note: Built into the Unreal Editor — no external bridge process. Enable via Edit > Plugins > "Unreal MCP" AND "All Toolsets" (both are required; the Toolset Registry dependency enables itself), then Edit > Editor Preferences > General > Model Context Protocol > toggle "Auto Start Server". The editor can also auto-generate a client config via the console command: ModelContextProtocol.GenerateClientConfig ClaudeCode. Endpoint, port, and path are configurable in Editor Preferences.
dataNote: Local HTTP/SSE connection to your own running Unreal Editor (127.0.0.1, no auth by default). No external/network calls beyond your machine.

name: Blender
description: Live Blender scene control from Claude - inspect the open scene, run Python (bpy) in your Blender session, render, and read the bundled Blender API and manual docs. Official Blender Foundation (Blender Lab) MCP server; needs Blender 5.1+.
summary: Live Blender scene control via the official Blender Lab MCP server (Blender 5.1+).
note: Official Blender Foundation (Blender Lab) MCP server, source-installed via uvx from projects.blender.org (pinned to release v1.0.3; needs the `uv` package manager and Python 3.10+). Requires Blender 5.1 or newer. In Blender, install the official MCP add-on from the Blender Lab extensions repository (https://lab.blender.org/; drag and drop the add-on into Blender, twice - first drop adds the repository, second installs the add-on - or use Install from Disk, see https://www.blender.org/lab/mcp-server/), enable it, and make sure its server is started (Preferences > Add-ons > MCP; it listens on local TCP port 9876 by default; the MCP process reads optional env BLENDER_MCP_HOST / BLENDER_MCP_PORT to match). SECURITY (Blender's own warning): the MCP server will execute LLM-generated code in Blender without any guards in place to protect your data from removal or being sent to a remote location. Use a virtual machine or a system without sensitive data, and back up your .blend first. If you previously installed the community 'MCP for Blender' add-on, disable it in Blender, since it uses the same port 9876, and turn off its telemetry. BLENDER_MCP_PORT changes the official server's port if needed.
dataNote: Runs locally over stdio and talks to the Blender add-on on localhost:9876. The first launch downloads the server and its Python dependencies from projects.blender.org and PyPI. The MCP server runs LLM-generated code in Blender unguarded.

name: Codex (OpenAI)
description: Adversarial review and second-opinion queries from OpenAI's Codex CLI, running as an MCP server — a non-Anthropic model for cross-checking plans, diffs, and reasoning. Exposes `codex` (new session) and `codex-reply` (continue a session) tools.
summary: Adversarial review and second opinions from OpenAI's Codex CLI running as an MCP server.
note: Local stdio MCP server launched via the bundled `.claude/hooks/codex-mcp-launcher.cjs` launcher (discovers the Codex binary and prefers a pinned `@openai/codex@0.153` install's `mcp-server` subcommand — removed in codex-cli 0.154+ — falling back automatically to `codex-app-server-mcp.cjs`, a shim over Codex's `app-server` protocol, when only a newer CLI is found). Installing hooks (Install Hooks button, or the portable/team install path) copies both scripts into your project's `.claude/hooks/`. Auth is via a ChatGPT subscription (shared rolling 5-hour quota across CLI/web/IDE use), not a metered API key — sign in once with `codex login`. The launch args below pin model and reasoning effort and set safe defaults for approval-policy and sandbox so this entry never silently inherits your global ~/.codex/config.toml (which may pin an expensive model at high reasoning effort). These are launch-time config.toml overrides (`-c key=value`); they set the SERVER's baked-in defaults, not a hard ceiling — the `codex` tool's own per-call `sandbox`/`approval-policy`/`model` arguments can still override them at call time, so a caller (or an untrusted prompt) can request a looser sandbox or a costlier model on an individual call. No separate flag exists to hard-lock per-call arguments; `-c` only sets the config.toml-equivalent default the server starts with. If model-slug errors surface (e.g. "model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account"), run `codex debug models` to list slugs actually accepted by your account.
dataNote: Prompts, code, and file contents you send through this server leave this machine and are sent to OpenAI's Codex/ChatGPT backend under your ChatGPT subscription. This is a different vendor than Anthropic and a different data-handling relationship than any Anthropic-run tool in this catalog.

name: Claude CLI
description: Route model calls through the user's own `claude` CLI login (a Claude Max/Pro subscription) instead of a metered Anthropic API key — a zero-dependency local MCP server wrapping `claude -p`. Exposes a single `claude` tool.
summary: Routes model calls through the user's own Claude CLI subscription instead of a metered API key.
note: Local stdio MCP server (hooks/claude-cli-mcp.cjs, run via `node`). Auth is entirely the user's existing `claude` CLI login — TycoonAgents never sees, stores, or forwards credentials; it just shells out to the CLI the user already signed into. This uses Anthropic's own supported CLI surface, never a third-party OAuth client impersonating one — Anthropic's terms restrict third-party OAuth against Claude, and this deliberately stays on the vendor's official path instead (not legal advice). Defaults: permission-mode 'plan' (read-only planning, no unattended edits) and a fresh scratch working directory per call so the caller's project CLAUDE.md is NOT auto-loaded (and its prompt-cache-creation cost avoided) unless `cwd` is set on purpose. Optional env overrides: CLAUDE_CLI_BIN (explicit binary path, skips discovery), CLAUDE_CLI_MODEL (default model id, default 'claude-haiku-4-5'), CLAUDE_CLI_PERMISSION_MODE (default 'plan'), CLAUDE_CLI_CWD (default working directory), CLAUDE_CLI_TIMEOUT_MS (default 180000). Verified against `claude --help` (Claude Code 2.1.258) for --model/--permission-mode/--allowedTools/--append-system-prompt/--output-format.
package: hooks/claude-cli-mcp.cjs (bundled with TycoonAgents; requires the `claude` CLI already installed and logged in)
dataNote: Prompts sent through this server go to Anthropic under the user's own Claude subscription, via the same `claude` CLI the user already uses interactively — no different a data relationship than using Claude Code directly.

name: Dart & Flutter
description: Analyze and fix Dart & Flutter code, resolve symbols, fetch API docs, search pub.dev, manage pubspec.yaml dependencies, run tests, and format code — via Google's official dart mcp-server.
summary: Analyzes and fixes Dart & Flutter code via Google's official dart mcp-server.
note: Provided by the Dart SDK — no separate install if `dart` (3.9+) is on your PATH. Best used inside a Flutter/Dart project (a directory with pubspec.yaml). If your MCP client has trouble with workspace roots, add "--force-roots-fallback" to args.
package: dart mcp-server (bundled with the Dart SDK 3.9+; run via `dart`)
dataNote: Runs locally against your project's Dart/Flutter source; contacts pub.dev when searching packages or fetching docs. Requires the Dart SDK (3.9+) on your PATH.

name: Gemini (Google)
description: Second-opinion / cross-vendor review queries against Google's Gemini models, running as an MCP server. Exposes `ask-gemini` (analyze/ask, optional sandbox mode), `sandbox-test`, and `ping` tools.
summary: Second-opinion, cross-vendor review queries against Google's Gemini models.
note: Google's own gemini-cli (https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli) only CONSUMES MCP servers — confirmed against its docs: it has no server-mode flag (no 'mcp-server'/'--experimental-mcp-server' subcommand), only a `mcpServers` client config in ~/.gemini/settings.json. There is no official Google-published Gemini MCP *server*. This entry instead uses the most-starred, actively-maintained community bridge, jamubc/gemini-mcp-tool (2.3k★, https://github.com/jamubc/gemini-mcp-tool), which runs the local `gemini` CLI under the hood and exposes it over MCP stdio. TycoonAgents runs it through its bundled wrapper (hooks/gemini-mcp-wrapper.cjs), which launches the PINNED version gemini-mcp-tool@1.1.8 via npx (the first run downloads that package from npm; its integrity hash is sha512-+tmm3hVAWkl+Orhymm54fz/gRs+bBX+GTFO5Eyb5lquOGEbJq3SxQKRhLHVrtq86W/X6edYn+taPu4RwG1ISuA== so you can verify it) (found on PATH; override with TYCOON_GEMINI_MCP_CMD) and returns a structured status (ok / provider_error / timeout / empty) with a timeout (TYCOON_BRIDGE_TIMEOUT_MS, default 180000) and a summary size cap (TYCOON_BRIDGE_MAX_CHARS, default 12000). Auth follows whatever the underlying `gemini` CLI is configured with — interactive OAuth login (`gemini` CLI's default) or, if you'd rather avoid a browser login step, the CLI's own support for reading GEMINI_API_KEY from the environment. Set GEMINI_API_KEY here only if you want that path; the server can also work with a CLI already logged in via OAuth (leave the value blank in that case). The `gemini` CLI itself must be installed and on PATH. UPDATE 2026-06-18: Google retired the Gemini CLI for individual users; gemini-mcp-tool now defaults to the Antigravity CLI (`agy`) backend. Set GEMINI_MCP_BACKEND=gemini to keep using the Gemini CLI (paid API key / enterprise), or GEMINI_MCP_BACKEND=agy for Antigravity (source: https://github.com/jamubc/gemini-mcp-tool). Install whichever CLI matches the backend you choose.
package: gemini-mcp-tool (community bridge over Google's gemini CLI, pinned 1.1.8, run via `npx` through the bundled wrapper)
dataNote: Prompts and content you send through this server leave this machine and are sent to Google's Gemini backend, via the local backend CLI's own auth (Antigravity `agy` by default, or `gemini` when GEMINI_MCP_BACKEND=gemini) (OAuth login or GEMINI_API_KEY). A different vendor than Anthropic, routed through a third-party (non-Google-published) MCP bridge rather than an official Gemini MCP server.

name: OpenAI-Compatible Endpoint
description: Call any OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint (a local vLLM/Ollama/LM Studio server, or a hosted OpenAI-compatible API such as Kimi or Qwen) through one MCP `chat` tool — for local or self-hosted models this project doesn't special-case.
summary: Calls any OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint through one MCP chat tool.
note: Zero-dependency MCP stdio server shipped with this project (hooks/openai-compatible-mcp.cjs) — nothing to install separately. Points at any server exposing a `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint: vLLM, Ollama (OpenAI-compatible mode), LM Studio, or a hosted OpenAI-compatible API like Moonshot's Kimi or Alibaba's Qwen — including one running on a remote VM, by pointing OPENAI_COMPAT_BASE_URL at its address. OPENAI_COMPAT_API_KEY is optional — omit it for a local server with no auth (e.g. Ollama/LM Studio on localhost); set it for a hosted or auth-gated endpoint. Exposes one tool, `chat`, taking {model, prompt, system?, messages?, max_tokens?}.
package: hooks/openai-compatible-mcp.cjs (bundled with this project, run via `node`)
dataNote: Prompts and content you send through this server go to whatever host OPENAI_COMPAT_BASE_URL points at — a fully local server (e.g. Ollama on localhost) never leaves this machine; a hosted endpoint (e.g. Kimi/Qwen) sends data to that vendor under your own account/key.

name: Supabase (Official)
description: Manage Supabase projects from Claude - query databases, apply migrations, and inspect logs via Supabase's official hosted MCP server.
summary: Supabase's official hosted MCP server for projects, databases, and migrations.
note: Official Supabase-hosted remote server - nothing to install locally. Authenticates with OAuth (dynamic client registration) in the browser on first use; no token to create. Optional URL query parameters: read_only=true (run queries as a read-only Postgres user) and project_ref=<id> (scope to one project). Prefer read_only=true and a non-production project. Source: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/getting-started/mcp
package: Supabase-hosted remote MCP server (no local install)
dataNote: Connects to Supabase's hosted MCP server using your authorized Supabase account; the model can read and change the projects and databases you grant.

name: Sentry (Official)
description: Search errors, inspect issues and performance data, and manage issues from Claude via Sentry's official hosted MCP server.
summary: Sentry's official hosted MCP server for errors, issues, and performance.
note: Official Sentry-hosted remote server - nothing to install locally. All connections use OAuth; the first connection triggers a browser sign-in to your Sentry account. To scope to one project, use https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp/<organizationSlug>/<projectSlug> in your own .mcp.json. Source: https://mcp.sentry.dev/
package: Sentry-hosted remote MCP server (no local install)
dataNote: Connects to Sentry's hosted MCP server using your authorized Sentry account; the model can read and manage the organizations and projects you grant.

name: Stripe (Official)
description: Interact with the Stripe API and search Stripe's docs from Claude via Stripe's official hosted MCP server.
summary: Stripe's official hosted MCP server for API access and docs search.
note: Official Stripe-hosted remote server - nothing to install locally. Authenticate with OAuth: run /mcp in Claude Code and authenticate Stripe. Use a sandbox while testing; Stripe asks for human confirmation before sensitive writes such as refunds. For non-interactive use, Stripe documents an agent API key sent as `Authorization: Bearer ${AGENT_API_KEY}` from an environment variable in your own .mcp.json (never commit the key); full-access secret keys and restricted keys without the Agent tag stop working on 2026-10-31. Source: https://docs.stripe.com/mcp
package: Stripe-hosted remote MCP server (no local install)
dataNote: Connects to Stripe's hosted MCP server using your authorized Stripe account; the model can read and, with confirmation for sensitive actions, change payments, customers, and billing data.

name: Figma (Official)
description: Bring Figma design context into Claude and write to the canvas via Figma's official hosted MCP server.
summary: Figma's official hosted MCP server for design context.
note: Official Figma-hosted remote server - nothing to install locally. Authenticates with OAuth: run /mcp in Claude Code, select figma, choose Authenticate, and click Allow Access. Figma lists the remote server as available on all seats and plans. Source: https://developers.figma.com/docs/figma-mcp-server/remote-server-installation/
package: Figma-hosted remote MCP server (no local install)
dataNote: Connects to Figma's hosted MCP server using your authorized Figma account; the model can read the design files you grant and write to the canvas.
